claim: FGF21 was labeled with molecularly defined gold nanoparticles (AuNPs).
source: The fibroblast growth factor FGF21 was labeled with molecularly defined gold nanoparticles (AuNPs), applied to human adipocytes, and imaged by cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET).
evidence: Described in the abstract as a methodological approach used in the study.

claim: Most AuNPs were in pairs about 80 Å apart on the outer cell surface.
source: Most AuNPs were in pairs about 80 Å apart, on the outer cell surface.
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-ET imaging data reported in the abstract.

claim: Pairs of AuNPs were abundant inside the cells in clathrin-coated vesicles and endosomes.
source: Pairs of AuNPs were also abundant inside the cells in clathrin-coated vesicles and endosomes.
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-ET imaging data reported in the abstract.

claim: AuNPs were present but no longer paired in multivesicular bodies.
source: AuNPs were present but no longer paired in multivesicular bodies.
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-ET imaging data reported in the abstract.

claim: FGF21 could be tracked along the endocytotic pathway.
source: FGF21 could thus be tracked along the endocytotic pathway.
evidence: Inference drawn from the observation of AuNP-labeled FGF21 in various cellular compartments.

claim: The methods developed can be applied to a wide variety of cargo.
source: The methods developed here to visualize signaling coupled to endocytosis can be applied to a wide variety of cargo and may be extended to studies of other intracellular transactions.
evidence: Speculative statement about the potential applicability of the method.

claim: The methods may be extended to studies of other intracellular transactions.
source: The methods developed here to visualize signaling coupled to endocytosis can be applied to a wide variety of cargo and may be extended to studies of other intracellular transactions.
evidence: Speculative statement about the potential applicability of the method.

claim: Fluorescence light microscopy has been performed at modest resolution on living cells in real time.
source: Imaging of cell structure has been performed using fluorescence light microscopy at modest resolution on living cells in real time, and using electron microscopy at higher resolution on fixed, embedded, sectioned material.
evidence: Statement based on established scientific knowledge about imaging techniques.

claim: Electron microscopy has been performed at higher resolution on fixed, embedded, sectioned material.
source: Imaging of cell structure has been performed using fluorescence light microscopy at modest resolution on living cells in real time, and using electron microscopy at higher resolution on fixed, embedded, sectioned material.
evidence: Statement based on established scientific knowledge about imaging techniques.

claim: The power of fluorescence light microscopy has been extended by super-resolution techniques.
source: The power of fluorescence light microscopy has been extended by super-resolution techniques (Baddeley and Bewersdorf, 2018), while advances in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) have yielded structures of purified proteins at near atomic resolution (Peplow, 2017), and have enhanced tomography of intact cells (Oikonomou and Jensen, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Baddeley and Bewersdorf, 2018.

claim: Advances in cryo-electron microscopy have yielded structures of purified proteins at near atomic resolution.
source: The power of fluorescence light microscopy has been extended by super-resolution techniques (Baddeley and Bewersdorf, 2018), while advances in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) have yielded structures of purified proteins at near atomic resolution (Peplow, 2017), and have enhanced tomography of intact cells (Oikonomou and Jensen, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Peplow, 2017.

claim: Advances in cryo-electron microscopy have enhanced tomography of intact cells.
source: The power of fluorescence light microscopy has been extended by super-resolution techniques (Baddeley and Bewersdorf, 2018), while advances in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) have yielded structures of purified proteins at near atomic resolution (Peplow, 2017), and have enhanced tomography of intact cells (Oikonomou and Jensen, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Oikonomou and Jensen, 2017.

claim: Cryo-ET provides an opportunity to study proteins as they interact with a myriad of other factors.
source: Cryo-ET provides an opportunity to study proteins as they interact with a myriad of other factors (Beck and Baumeister, 2016; Irobalieva et al., 2016), often lost during protein purification.
evidence: Supported by citations to Beck and Baumeister, 2016 and Irobalieva et al., 2016.

claim: Factors that proteins interact with are often lost during protein purification.
source: Cryo-ET provides an opportunity to study proteins as they interact with a myriad of other factors (Beck and Baumeister, 2016; Irobalieva et al., 2016), often lost during protein purification.
evidence: Statement based on established knowledge about protein purification.

claim: Very large multi-protein assemblies, such as ribosomes and chemoreceptor arrays, scatter electrons strongly enough that they can be recognized in electron micrographs of frozen hydrated specimens.
source: Very large multi-protein assemblies, such as ribosomes and chemoreceptor arrays, scatter electrons strongly enough that they can be recognized in electron micrographs of frozen hydrated specimens (Briegel and Jensen, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Briegel and Jensen, 2017.

claim: The AuNP conjugate approach enables the identification and image processing of most molecules and molecular assemblies, which are too small to be detected against the background of scattering from the cellular milieu.
source: Our approach, employing AuNP conjugates, enables the identification and image processing of most molecules and molecular assemblies, which are too small to be detected against the background of scattering from the cellular milieu.
evidence: Inference based on the methodological approach described in the study.

claim: Defined heavy atom clusters have been developed and targeted to individual molecules.
source: To that end, we have developed defined heavy atom clusters, targeted to individual molecules (Azubel and Kornberg, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Azubel and Kornberg, 2016.

claim: FGFs are essential in cell biology through their participation in cell proliferation, cell survival and cell motility (paracrine FGFs).
source: FGFs are essential in cell biology, either by their participation in cell proliferation, cell survival and cell motility (paracrine FGFs), or by their connection to metabolic processes (endocrine FGFs).
evidence: Statement based on established scientific knowledge about FGFs.

claim: FGFs are essential in cell biology through their connection to metabolic processes (endocrine FGFs).
source: FGFs are essential in cell biology, either by their participation in cell proliferation, cell survival and cell motility (paracrine FGFs), or by their connection to metabolic processes (endocrine FGFs).
evidence: Statement based on established scientific knowledge about FGFs.

claim: Paracrine and endocrine FGFs share a common first step: binding of FGFs to cell membrane receptors.
source: These diverse activities share a common first step: binding of FGFs to cell membrane receptors.
evidence: Statement based on established scientific knowledge about FGF signaling.

claim: There are four genes for FGF receptors (FGFRs), which produce seven alternatively spliced variants.
source: There are four genes for FGF receptors (FGFRs), which produce seven alternatively spliced variants.
evidence: Statement based on established scientific knowledge about FGFRs.

claim: Paracrine and endocrine FGFs, totaling 15 and three secreted proteins, respectively, compete for binding to seven FGFRs.
source: Paracrine and endocrine FGFs, totaling 15 and three secreted proteins, respectively, compete for binding to these seven FGFRs (Ornitz and Itoh, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ornitz and Itoh, 2015.

claim: Paracrine FGFs are assisted by heparan sulfate for binding.
source: Binding requires co-factors: paracrine FGFs are assisted by heparan sulfate, and endocrine FGFs by either αKlotho or βKlotho (Kilkenny and Rocheleau, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kilkenny and Rocheleau, 2016.

claim: Endocrine FGFs are assisted by either αKlotho or βKlotho for binding.
source: Binding requires co-factors: paracrine FGFs are assisted by heparan sulfate, and endocrine FGFs by either αKlotho or βKlotho (Kilkenny and Rocheleau, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kilkenny and Rocheleau, 2016.

claim: Binding leads to FGFR dimerization and activation of FGFR tyrosine kinase activity.
source: Binding leads to FGFR dimerization and activation of FGFR tyrosine kinase activity, which triggers RAS-MAPK, PI3K-AKT, and PLCγ1 signaling cascades (Ornitz and Itoh, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ornitz and Itoh, 2015.

claim: FGFR tyrosine kinase activity triggers RAS-MAPK, PI3K-AKT, and PLCγ1 signaling cascades.
source: Binding leads to FGFR dimerization and activation of FGFR tyrosine kinase activity, which triggers RAS-MAPK, PI3K-AKT, and PLCγ1 signaling cascades (Ornitz and Itoh, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ornitz and Itoh, 2015.

claim: Signaling is commonly thought to occur at the cell surface.
source: Whereas signaling is commonly thought to occur at the cell surface, it continues in endosomal locations (Jean et al., 2010) (Haugsten et al., 2011).
evidence: Statement about common scientific understanding.

claim: Signaling continues in endosomal locations.
source: Whereas signaling is commonly thought to occur at the cell surface, it continues in endosomal locations (Jean et al., 2010) (Haugsten et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jean et al., 2010 and Haugsten et al., 2011.

claim: Signaling cascades are interrupted when endocytosis is inhibited.
source: Moreover, signaling cascades are interrupted when endocytosis is inhibited (Yaqoob et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yaqoob et al., 2014.

claim: Endocytosis modulates signaling.
source: Endocytosis modulates signaling, as the specific endocytic pathway (Mayor and Pagano, 2007) determines whether the receptor is recycled to the cell surface or destined for degradation (Haugsten et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to Mayor and Pagano, 2007 and Haugsten et al., 2005.

claim: The specific endocytic pathway determines whether the receptor is recycled to the cell surface or destined for degradation.
source: Endocytosis modulates signaling, as the specific endocytic pathway (Mayor and Pagano, 2007) determines whether the receptor is recycled to the cell surface or destined for degradation (Haugsten et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to Mayor and Pagano, 2007 and Haugsten et al., 2005.

claim: Signaling must be studied in the context of membrane internalization and vesicle trafficking.
source: Signaling must therefore be studied in the context of membrane internalization and vesicle trafficking.
evidence: Inference drawn from the relationship between signaling and endocytosis.

claim: A fundamental question regarding the activation of the signaling cascade is the stoichiometry of the ternary complex (FGF-receptor-cofactor).
source: A fundamental question regarding the activation of the signaling cascade is the stochiometry of the ternary complex (FGF-receptor-cofactor).
evidence: Statement identifying an open scientific question.

claim: Competing models for the stoichiometry of the ternary complex have been proposed.
source: Competing models have been proposed (Goetz and Mohammadi, 2013; Yie et al., 2012) (Pomin, 2016) (Kilkenny and Rocheleau, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Goetz and Mohammadi, 2013; Yie et al., 2012; Pomin, 2016; and Kilkenny and Rocheleau, 2016.

claim: The crystal structure of FGF2-FGFR1c (extracellular domains D2-D3) and heparan sulfate showed a 2:2:2 ternary complex.
source: The crystal structure of FGF2-FGFR1c (extracellular domains D2-D3) and heparan sulfate showed a 2:2:2 ternary complex (Schlessinger et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Schlessinger et al., 2000.

claim: αKlotho and βKlotho differ significantly in both size and shape from heparan sulfate.
source: αKlotho and βKlotho differ significantly in both size and shape from heparan sulfate, and also compete with some paracrine FGFs for the same regions to bind receptors (Goetz and Mohammadi, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Goetz and Mohammadi, 2013.

claim: αKlotho and βKlotho compete with some paracrine FGFs for the same regions to bind receptors.
source: αKlotho and βKlotho differ significantly in both size and shape from heparan sulfate, and also compete with some paracrine FGFs for the same regions to bind receptors (Goetz and Mohammadi, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Goetz and Mohammadi, 2013.

claim: A different mode of binding that could lead to a different stoichiometry for endocrine ternary complexes could not be ruled out.
source: Thus a different mode of binding that could lead to a different stochiometry for endocrine ternary complexes could not be ruled out.
evidence: Inference based on structural differences between cofactors.

claim: Subsequent studies of FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho have favored a 1:2:1 model.
source: Indeed, subsequent studies of FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho have favored a 1:2:1 model (Ming et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ming et al., 2012.

claim: The crystal structure of a 1:1:1 complex of membrane proximal portion of extracellular FGFR1c, soluble αKlotho, and FGF23 was described.
source: Most recently, the crystal structure of a 1:1:1 complex of membrane proximal portion of extracellular FGFR1c, soluble αKlotho, and FGF23 was described, and dimerization of the αKlotho complex was observed in the presence of heparan (Chen et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2018.

claim: Dimerization of the αKlotho complex was observed in the presence of heparan.
source: Most recently, the crystal structure of a 1:1:1 complex of membrane proximal portion of extracellular FGFR1c, soluble αKlotho, and FGF23 was described, and dimerization of the αKlotho complex was observed in the presence of heparan (Chen et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2018.

claim: The extracellular domain of βKlotho bound to the C-terminus of FGF21 was determined by X-ray crystallography, revealing a 1:1 complex.
source: The extracellular domain of βKlotho bound to the C-terminus of FGF21 was also determined by X-ray crystallography, revealing a 1:1 complex, suggested to lead to an overall 2:2:2 complex (Lee et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lee et al., 2018.

claim: The 1:1 complex of βKlotho and FGF21 was suggested to lead to an overall 2:2:2 complex.
source: The extracellular domain of βKlotho bound to the C-terminus of FGF21 was also determined by X-ray crystallography, revealing a 1:1 complex, suggested to lead to an overall 2:2:2 complex (Lee et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lee et al., 2018.

claim: FGF21 has emerged as a potential candidate for treatment of obesity and type II diabetes.
source: In recent years, FGF21 has emerged as a potential candidate for treatment of obesity and type II diabetes (Kharitonenkov and DiMarchi, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kharitonenkov and DiMarchi, 2015.

claim: Pleiotropy of FGF21 includes effects on glucose and lipid metabolism in adipocyte tissue.
source: Pleiotropy of FGF21 includes effects on glucose and lipid metabolism in adipocyte tissue (Degirolamo et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Degirolamo et al., 2016.

claim: FGF21 signals through FGFR1c, FGFR2c and FGFR3c, provided that βKlotho is accessible.
source: FGF21 signals through FGFR1c, FGFR2c and FGFR3c, provided that βKlotho is accessible (Kilkenny and Rocheleau, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kilkenny and Rocheleau, 2016.

claim: Both FGFR1c and βKlotho are endogenously expressed in adipocyte tissue.
source: Both FGFR1c and βKlotho are endogenously expressed in adipocyte tissue.
evidence: Statement based on established knowledge about adipocyte tissue.

claim: The pathway of FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho complex internalization remains an open question.
source: The pathway of FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho complex internalization remains an open question.
evidence: Statement identifying an open scientific question.

claim: Evidence for both clathrin-dependent and clathrin-independent pathways, for different combinations of FGF and FGFR, has been presented.
source: Evidence for both clathrin-dependent (Jean et al.) and clathrin-independent (Haugsten et al., 2011) pathways, for different combinations of FGF and FGFR, has been presented.
evidence: Supported by citations to Jean et al. and Haugsten et al., 2011.

claim: Dynamin-dependent endocytosis has been suggested for the FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho complex.
source: Regarding the FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho complex, dynamin-dependent endocytosis has been suggested (Yaqoob et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yaqoob et al., 2014.

claim: Dynamin has been found associated to both clathrin-dependent and clathrin-independent endocytosis.
source: However, dynamin has been found associated to both clathrin-dependent and clathrin-independent endocytosis (Mayor and Pagano, 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Mayor and Pagano, 2007.

claim: Different states of activation, internalization, and traffic of the FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho ternary complex were captured using gold-labeled FGF21 and cryo-ET.
source: With the use of gold-labeled FGF21 (AuNP-FGF21) and cryo-ET, we captured different states of activation, internalization, and traffic of the FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho ternary complex, from binding and complex formation at the cell surface, to coated pits, to coated vesicles, to endosomes, and finally, to multivesicular bodies, in which the complexes were disrupted.
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-ET imaging data.

claim: The FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho ternary complex was observed from binding and complex formation at the cell surface, to coated pits, to coated vesicles, to endosomes, and finally, to multivesicular bodies.
source: With the use of gold-labeled FGF21 (AuNP-FGF21) and cryo-ET, we captured different states of activation, internalization, and traffic of the FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho ternary complex, from binding and complex formation at the cell surface, to coated pits, to coated vesicles, to endosomes, and finally, to multivesicular bodies, in which the complexes were disrupted.
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-ET imaging data.

claim: The FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho complexes were disrupted in multivesicular bodies.
source: With the use of gold-labeled FGF21 (AuNP-FGF21) and cryo-ET, we captured different states of activation, internalization, and traffic of the FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho ternary complex, from binding and complex formation at the cell surface, to coated pits, to coated vesicles, to endosomes, and finally, to multivesicular bodies, in which the complexes were disrupted.
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-ET imaging data.

claim: The observations are clearly indicative of clathrin-dependent endocytosis.
source: These observations are clearly indicative of clathrin-dependent endocytosis.
evidence: Inference drawn from the observation of AuNP-labeled FGF21 in clathrin-coated structures.

claim: Subtomogram averaging and helical reconstruction revealed structures of putative AAA+ ATPases, actin filaments, and microtubules.
source: Finally, subtomogram averaging and helical reconstruction revealed structures of other important components, including putative AAA+ ATPases, actin filaments, and microtubules, giving a three-dimensional picture of the entire pathway.
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-ET imaging data and computational analysis.

claim: The structures revealed give a three-dimensional picture of the entire pathway.
source: Finally, subtomogram averaging and helical reconstruction revealed structures of other important components, including putative AAA+ ATPases, actin filaments, and microtubules, giving a three-dimensional picture of the entire pathway.
evidence: Inference based on the comprehensive structural data obtained.

claim: A 144-gold atom nanoparticle (AuNP) was conjugated with an FGF21 variant bearing a surface-exposed cysteine residue.
source: A 144-gold atom nanoparticle (AuNP) was conjugated with an FGF21 variant bearing a surface-exposed cysteine residue (Xu et al., 2013), as described (Azubel and Kornberg, 2016).
evidence: Methodological description supported by citations to Xu et al., 2013 and Azubel and Kornberg, 2016.

claim: Interaction in ternary complexes was assessed using membrane preparations from three cell sources: parental CHO cells, transformed CHO cells overexpressing βKlotho and FGFR1c or only βKlotho, and human primary adipocytes.
source: Interaction in ternary complexes was assessed using membrane preparations from three cell sources: parental CHO cells, in which neither FGFR1c nor βKlotho are expressed; transformed CHO cells overexpressing βKlotho and FGFR1c or only βKlotho; and human primary adipocytes, in which βKlotho and FGFR1c are endogenously expressed.
evidence: Methodological description of experimental design.

claim: Neither FGFR1c nor βKlotho are expressed in parental CHO cells.
source: Interaction in ternary complexes was assessed using membrane preparations from three cell sources: parental CHO cells, in which neither FGFR1c nor βKlotho are expressed; transformed CHO cells overexpressing βKlotho and FGFR1c or only βKlotho; and human primary adipocytes, in which βKlotho and FGFR1c are endogenously expressed.
evidence: Statement about the characteristics of the cell line used.

claim: βKlotho and FGFR1c are endogenously expressed in human primary adipocytes.
source: Interaction in ternary complexes was assessed using membrane preparations from three cell sources: parental CHO cells, in which neither FGFR1c nor βKlotho are expressed; transformed CHO cells overexpressing βKlotho and FGFR1c or only βKlotho; and human primary adipocytes, in which βKlotho and FGFR1c are endogenously expressed.
evidence: Statement about the characteristics of the cell type used.

claim: Vesicles were treated at 4°C with either AuNP-FGF21 or a gold-labeled single chain antibody fragment (AuNP-scFv) that binds βKlotho.
source: Vesicles were treated at 4°C with either AuNP-FGF21 or a gold-labeled single chain antibody fragment (AuNP-scFv) that binds βKlotho, and washed to remove unbound gold conjugate.
evidence: Methodological description of experimental procedure.

claim: Micrographs of vesicles from parental CHO cells membrane preparations treated with AuNP-FGF21 showed no associated AuNPs.
source: Micrographs of vesicles from parental CHO cells membrane preparations treated with AuNP-FGF21 showed no associated AuNPs, whereas micrographs of vesicles from primary adipocytes membrane preparations treated with AuNP-FGF21 showed pairs of AuNPs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-EM imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Micrographs of vesicles from primary adipocytes membrane preparations treated with AuNP-FGF21 showed pairs of AuNPs.
source: Micrographs of vesicles from parental CHO cells membrane preparations treated with AuNP-FGF21 showed no associated AuNPs, whereas micrographs of vesicles from primary adipocytes membrane preparations treated with AuNP-FGF21 showed pairs of AuNPs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-EM imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: AuNPs were distinguishable from other particles because of an effect of the contrast transfer function, producing a bright halo around the strongly scattering gold core.
source: AuNPs were distinguishable from other particles because of an effect of the contrast transfer function, producing a bright halo around the strongly scattering gold core (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Explanation of how AuNPs were identified in the images, supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Pairing of particles cannot be determined from 2D images alone, as two particles in close proximity in the x-y plane may be far apart in z.
source: Pairing of particles cannot be determined from 2D images alone, as two particles in close proximity in the x-y plane may be far apart in z.
evidence: Statement based on the principles of 3D imaging.

claim: 85% of AuNPs were in true pairs in membrane preparations from CHO cells overexpressing βKlotho and FGFR1c treated with AuNP-FGF21.
source: Tilt series were therefore collected for membrane preparations from CHO cells overexpressing βKlotho and FGFR1c treated with AuNP-FGF21, followed by tomographic reconstruction, showing that 85% of AuNPs were in true pairs (Figure 1—figure supplement 3a–g), indicative of two copies of FGF21 in the receptor complex.
evidence: Direct observation from tomographic reconstruction data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3a–g.

claim: 85% of AuNPs in true pairs is indicative of two copies of FGF21 in the receptor complex.
source: Tilt series were therefore collected for membrane preparations from CHO cells overexpressing βKlotho and FGFR1c treated with AuNP-FGF21, followed by tomographic reconstruction, showing that 85% of AuNPs were in true pairs (Figure 1—figure supplement 3a–g), indicative of two copies of FGF21 in the receptor complex.
evidence: Inference drawn from the observation of paired AuNPs.

claim: Treatment of CHO membrane vesicles with AuNP-scFv against βKlotho resulted in a high percentage of pairs of particles.
source: Treatment of these CHO membrane vesicles with AuNP-scFv against βKlotho also resulted in a high percentage of pairs of particles (Figure 1—figure supplement 3h), indicative of an overall 2:2:2 stoichometry for the receptor complex.
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-EM imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3h.

claim: A high percentage of pairs of particles with AuNP-scFv against βKlotho is indicative of an overall 2:2:2 stoichiometry for the receptor complex.
source: Treatment of these CHO membrane vesicles with AuNP-scFv against βKlotho also resulted in a high percentage of pairs of particles (Figure 1—figure supplement 3h), indicative of an overall 2:2:2 stoichometry for the receptor complex.
evidence: Inference drawn from the observation of paired AuNPs with both FGF21 and βKlotho labeling.

claim: Pairs of particles were not observed when membrane preparations from CHO cells expressing only βKlotho were treated with AuNP-scFv against βKlotho.
source: When membrane preparations from CHO cells expressing only βKlotho were treated with AuNP-scFv against βKlotho, pairs of particles were not observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 3j), showing that βKlotho did not dimerize on its own.
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-EM imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3j.

claim: βKlotho did not dimerize on its own.
source: When membrane preparations from CHO cells expressing only βKlotho were treated with AuNP-scFv against βKlotho, pairs of particles were not observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 3j), showing that βKlotho did not dimerize on its own.
evidence: Inference drawn from the absence of paired AuNPs in the absence of receptor.

claim: Pairs of particles were observed when CHO cells expressing only βKlotho were treated with AuNP-FGF21.
source: When the same vesicles were treated with AuNP-FGF21, however, pairs of particles were again observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 3i).
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-EM imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3i.

claim: Either two molecules of FGF21 bind to one βKlotho, or FGF21 induces dimerization of overexpressed βKlotho, even in the absence of receptor.
source: Either two molecules of FGF21 bind to one βKlotho, or FGF21 induces dimerization of overexpressed βKlotho, even in the absence of receptor.
evidence: Inference drawn from the observation of paired AuNPs in the absence of receptor.

claim: Overexpression of FGFR1c and βKlotho may lead to receptor auto-activation.
source: Because overexpression of FGFR1c and βKlotho may lead to receptor auto-activation (Sørensen et al., 2006), and with a view to studies on intact cells (see below), we repeated the analysis with AuNP-FGF21 on membrane preparations from human adipocytes.
evidence: Supported by citation to Sørensen et al., 2006.

claim: 89% of AuNPs were in true pairs in membrane preparations from human adipocytes treated with AuNP-FGF21.
source: As before, tilt series were collected, followed by tomographic reconstruction, revealing 89% of AuNPs in true pairs, with an average separation (center-to-center distance) of 80 ± 15 Å (Figure 1).
evidence: Direct observation from tomographic reconstruction data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The average separation (center-to-center distance) of AuNP pairs in membrane preparations from human adipocytes was 80 ± 15 Å.
source: As before, tilt series were collected, followed by tomographic reconstruction, revealing 89% of AuNPs in true pairs, with an average separation (center-to-center distance) of 80 ± 15 Å (Figure 1).
evidence: Direct measurement from tomographic reconstruction data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Use of the AuNPs improved the alignment of the tilt series.
source: With use of the AuNPs to improve the alignment of the tilt series (Figure 1—figure supplement 4), protein densities on both inner and outer surfaces of the membrane were revealed (Figure 1a and Figure 1—figure supplement 4c).
evidence: Methodological observation supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Protein densities on both inner and outer surfaces of the membrane were revealed.
source: With use of the AuNPs to improve the alignment of the tilt series (Figure 1—figure supplement 4), protein densities on both inner and outer surfaces of the membrane were revealed (Figure 1a and Figure 1—figure supplement 4c).
evidence: Direct observation from tomographic reconstruction data shown in Figure 1a and Figure 1—figure supplement 4c.

claim: A key requirement for extension of the analysis to intact cells is sufficient thinness of the cells for cryo-EM.
source: A key requirement for extension of the analysis to intact cells is sufficient thinness of the cells for cryo-EM.
evidence: Statement based on technical requirements of cryo-EM.

claim: CHO cells were not well suited for cryo-EM due to insufficient thinness.
source: CHO cells were not well suited in this regard, but cytoplasmic regions of adipocyte cells grown on Holey-Carbon Au mesh grids were as thin as 200–300 nm near the cell periphery (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Observation about cell characteristics supported by Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cytoplasmic regions of adipocyte cells grown on Holey-Carbon Au mesh grids were as thin as 200–300 nm near the cell periphery.
source: CHO cells were not well suited in this regard, but cytoplasmic regions of adipocyte cells grown on Holey-Carbon Au mesh grids were as thin as 200–300 nm near the cell periphery (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Direct measurement from cryo-EM imaging data shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: 88% of AuNP particles were in pairs on the adipocyte cell surface.
source: As in the case of vesicles from CHO and adipocyte cells membrane preparations, most AuNP particles were in pairs (88%) on the adipocyte cell surface (Figure 3).
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-ET imaging data shown in Figure 3.

claim: AuNP pairs showed a tendency to cluster.
source: AuNP pairs showed a tendency to cluster, consistent with previous reports of clustering of FGF receptors from immunofluorescence studies with anti-FGFR antibodies (Gao et al., 2015).
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-ET imaging data, supported by citation to Gao et al., 2015.

claim: Clustering of FGF receptors has been reported from immunofluorescence studies with anti-FGFR antibodies.
source: AuNP pairs showed a tendency to cluster, consistent with previous reports of clustering of FGF receptors from immunofluorescence studies with anti-FGFR antibodies (Gao et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gao et al., 2015.

claim: AuNP pairs were found in areas surrounding filipodia.
source: AuNP pairs were found in areas surrounding filipodia and, most notably, above invaginations of the cell surface membrane with clathrin nets beneath (Figures 2 and 3).
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-ET imaging data shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: AuNP pairs were found above invaginations of the cell surface membrane with clathrin nets beneath.
source: AuNP pairs were found in areas surrounding filipodia and, most notably, above invaginations of the cell surface membrane with clathrin nets beneath (Figures 2 and 3).
evidence: Direct observation from cryo-ET imaging data shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: The occurrence of most AuNP-FGF21 in pairs pertains to the stoichiometry of the ternary complex.
source: The occurrence of most AuNP-FGF21 in pairs pertains to the stoichiometry of the ternary complex.
evidence: Inference drawn from the observation of paired AuNPs.

claim: The findings are suggestive of the occurrence of 2:2:2 FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho complexes in vivo.
source: Our findings are suggestive of the occurrence of 2:2:2 FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho complexes in vivo.
evidence: Inference drawn from the observation of paired AuNPs in intact cells.

claim: A number of familiar structures were visible in the tomograms of adipocyte cells: membranes, clathrin nets, actin filaments, microtubules, and hexameric rings.

claim: NSF and Vps4p, with similar structures to p97 AAA+ ATPase, could not be excluded as the identity of the hexameric rings.

claim: AuNPs in clathrin-coated vesicles and endosomes were invariably adjacent to the inner membrane surface.
source: Not only were almost all AuNPs paired in both clathrin-coated vesicles and endosomes (89% and 88%, respectively), but they were also invariably adjacent to the inner membrane surface, pointing to persistence of the FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho complex.

source: Finally, after overnight incubation at 37°C, AuNPs were observed in multivesicular bodies (MVBs).

source: Among 44 AuNPs observed inside five MVBs in different cells, no two AuNPs were closer than 250 Å to one another.

claim: The unpaired and membrane-unassociated state of AuNPs in MVBs indicates the disruption of the FGF21-FGFR1c-βKlotho complex in MVBs.
